protocol_reference.usage_note: All correct-path decisions follow the Airway-Breathing-Circulation-Disability-Exposure assessment order. Options that skip or delay airway/breathing assessment are penalized.

recoverability_rule.explanation: Resolves outcome_if_prior_state_recoverable vs outcome_if_prior_state_unrecoverable. Only ARREST (full cardiac arrest already reached before this decision) is unrecoverable -- even the optimal option D4:A cannot guarantee stabilization from ARREST within this simulation. Every other prior status (UNSTABLE_RECOVERING, DETERIORATING, CRITICAL, PERI_ARREST) is recoverable: choosing the optimal D4 option resolves it to STABILIZED regardless of how bad the trend was before this final decision. In other words, a patient's fate is decided by the quality of the LAST decision made, not by how many earlier mistakes preceded it -- a player who erred early but corrects course at D4 still saves the patient (see example_player_trajectories.player_B_mistake_then_recovers).

UNSTABLE_RECOVERING: Doctor, his condition is improving, but he remains unstable.
What would you like to do next?
DETERIORATING: Doctor, he still hasn't turned the corner.
CRITICAL: This is our last opportunity to stabilize him.
PERI_ARREST: Doctor, he's peri-arrest -- we need definitive action now.
ARREST: Doctor, he has arrested. We need to begin resuscitation immediately.

flow_control.explanation: Single-patient level. Every option's next_decision points only to another node for the same patient (P1), never elsewhere. The engine moves forward strictly by following the next_decision chosen by the player's selected option -- D1_INITIAL_RESPONSE -> D2_* (state-dependent) -> D3_* (state-dependent) -> D4_FINAL_MANAGEMENT -> ending. There is no next patient in this level.

sequence.on_complete: level complete once D4_FINAL_MANAGEMENT resolves to an ending in endings{}
